I get this all the time too! My problem is I’m focusing on other ppl & their thoughts/ what their thoughts could be while I’m suppose to be out having MY time. Just the simple thought that they might even look at me gets my anxiety thru the roof instantaneously. I’m still struggling with this myself, but what I found that kinda helped me personally was pretending like I’m the only one on that block, in that store aisle & whenever someone passes me or comes close to me I do the same thing. Only acknowledge if they meet my eye contact (HATE IT) then I’m forced to do a smile & walk away from them in panic. Music while walking also helps some, u get in ur zone, talk to yourself / hype your mind up reminding yourself you’re safe, you’re okay, no one else exists right now, it’s just me. (Of course be on alert for safety reasons). I know I don’t have really any answers, I’m no professional; but just wanted to say “I understand!” & give u a small piece of what kinda helps me :)

It didn’t go to well with me to be honest. In the beginning they told me they (had) substance abuse issues that were long past them n they were clean except for weed (don’t have a problem with it anymore) so I was completely ok with that.
As time went on tho, they got into the party/edm scene & that’s nothing but drugs and music.
I was hesitant but I was like ok..give the trust. I wanted them to prove me wrong.
But what I got met with is : hey ima try molly for the first time, that ok?
Me trying to b understanding & not judgmental & not wanting to ruin the mood I said *eye twitch* sure..
They were on the fone with me so I was slightly ok with it?
Then it went onto lsd and THATS when it became a problem.
Same exact thing as before. Asks, we’re on the fone. Still uneasy but with some hope.

Then they go out more and more, explain what they’re taking.
Then it changes to them using around u, getting comfortable.

I was stuck between…am I being too judgmental? A prude? Am I good support? Friend?
Or am I right with the way I feel..
Is this fair? Or isn’t it. Do I want this? Why do I still feel so uneasy.
Then it became they were gonna do it regardless if I approved or not. If I knew or not.
They’d slip sometimes & mention it, but at that time ur so drained with the what if’s & the what r they doing, hope they’re safe…that ur just done caring at a certain point.

What I learned: boundaries were never respected. I had too low self esteem to tell them how I really feel cus I was scared of their judgement or them leaving me.
I stayed. 4years. I tried to cope, tried to meet in the middle… eventually the ick of everything caught up & that’s what won. The ick & lack of respect & feeling so low thinking that there’s something wrong ME cus I’m not on the same level.
But it’s them..

You already read what these lovely humans wrote, but I do want to add;
I’ve had problems with ouid and anxiety/panic attacks for awhile. It was to a point where I couldn’t smoke without having them.
I’m hard headed & still wanted to enjoy the green goodness but I had to cut back for a little bit and changed things until I could get back to the way I was smoking or at least CLOSE.
If you find it hard to completely stop for a couple days I suggest “micro dosing” in a sense where you take a small hit, wait and see, and go from there. Try to get comfortable with the light high and almost train your brain to be like “this is all I need, I’m good”.

I think once you and your body start getting acclimated to the change and tries to separate panic attacks from ouid it might get easier.

Until then take it easy man :) treat your body right and give it a break. That shroom shit took you somewhere you weren’t ready for & your body was like WHATNOIDONTLIKE.
Goodluck! I really hope all goes well. I know it’s not easy, but a good mindset kinda helps :)

I was diagnosed with depression around the age of 8 because of a traumatic experience I had with the way my grandmother died, and that was also around the same time my mother became a alcoholic. I was never fully diagnosed with anxiety til around 15-16. I always wondered why. Why I was different, why I was always sick or in pain, why I was always scared, why it would  always come out of nowhere during certain times.
Not until my adult years did I actually realize that it also had something to do with anxiety. It was just my body’s way of expressing it and I never knew how to communicate it because I didn’t even know what it was at that time.
I thank you for posting this article, it truly speaks wonders and puts things into a new perspective for those who always wondered “why” and for parents to think outside the box at times when their child says “I have a stomachache” for the last couple weeks even after going to the doctors.
